body: I tested some other things in the code and noticed that this behavior occurs in an empty project without window settings. It can also appear in any corner of the screen. But I don’t understand why this happens, and it seems the issue is not with focus but with the initial window position - it’s clearly not centered, even though it should be.

I tried to reproduce this in 4.4.1.stable on win10 but no success. What os are you using? You've said that you tested it outside of the editor and that bug is still there, on both linux and windows - are you dualbooting or using something like wine to run the exported build for a different os?

> I tried to reproduce this in 4.4.1.stable on win10 but no success. What os are you using? You've said that you tested it outside of the editor and that bug is still there, on both linux and windows - are you dualbooting or using something like wine to run the exported build for a different os?

Currently, I’m using X11 on Linux, and in version 4.5.dev2 this issue definitely exists. I use Wine and Steam Proton to test the Windows version, and it happens there too. As far as I know and understand, if the build is made for a Windows release, it uses Windows-specific mechanisms => the emulation works exactly as it would if you ran it on Windows. I might be mistaken in how this works - feel free to correct me - but I believe the behavior is identical.

As for version 4.4.1.stable, I used to have it, but I’m no longer using that version, so I can’t say anything for sure, except that I did encounter the issue. Overall, regarding this specific problem, it’s hard to say whether it occurs on Windows - maybe it’s only on Linux in version 4.4.1.stable - but in version 4.5.dev2 it happens on both platforms, as I mentioned above.

As for this issue, I still haven't figured out why it's happening. It doesn't always occur - sometimes it's there, and other times everything works fine. Or everything is fine when you create a new project, and then it starts happening, as if something overflows and the window position changes. Initially, I thought it was related to focus, but it’s not. My current theory is this: the engine wants to create the window and starts the first rendering in the top-left corner of the screen, then moves it to the center. That’s a common practice for window creation, although in my experience with GLFW, SDL, and some other libraries, you could render the window centered right from the start. You can clearly see this behavior in the provided video.

The problem is: I can’t figure out why the engine sometimes renders the window from the center immediately, and other times from a corner. Moreover, it may use any of the four corners of the screen for this - even though the position is set to center. For example, yesterday before your comment, I created an issue where my window appeared in the bottom-left corner, although sometimes it’s in other corners or correctly in the center.

> As far as I know and understand, if the build is made for a Windows release, it uses Windows-specific mechanisms => the emulation works exactly as it would if you ran it on Windows. I might be mistaken in how this works - feel free to correct me - but I believe the behavior is identical.

Nope emulation is almost never 1 to 1, some os specific issues can still happen even behind a layer of emulation.

Anyways, i tried testing it on v4.5.dev2.official [af2c713]. Again - nothing like what you described and uploaded to youtube can be observed on windows 10. Must be a bug on Linux or with X11. Someone else needs to try replicate this on their own linux machine to rule out the possibility of a local problem.

Yes, I agree with you. It's just that I feel like the window position has always behaved consistently, even under emulation. I base this on the fact that everything Godot does in a Windows build exactly matches the behavior I can reproduce manually, which leads me to believe that window positioning, specifically, works identically.

Again, I'm saying this issue is hard to reproduce. When I first encountered it, I had to relaunch the window many times to trigger it, and later it started appearing sporadically, which allowed me to record it. It's still unclear to me - I can launch a new project on v4.5.dev2 right now and the issue might not show up at all. I don't even know how to reliably reproduce it except by restarting the window.

So even though you've tested it on Windows, are you completely sure? Hopefully, it's just an X11 issue - that would make it significantly easier to resolve.
Yeah i'm sure about it not being present on windows. Mysterious shit ngl

Couldn't replicate on Fedora Linux 42 ( Workstation Edition ) v4.4.1.stable.official

Both on XWayland ( https://youtu.be/rOYE1ViSCHU ) and Wayland ( https://youtu.be/d0M3J4K9kuU ). (Still needs to be tested on x11 by someone else)

Edit: Forgot to mention that I did the steps for a couple of minutes off-camera both on XWayland and Wayland

On v4.5.beta5.official [c81fd6c51], I still have this, even though I’ve been working on other projects in the meantime. In the images, I captured the start of the launch — the window just spawns in any of the four corners, but for some reason, right now, for example, it always spawns in the bottom-left one. I would understand if it were at least the top-right. And then it just centers itself. Although again, according to all the settings, it should be there from the start. Yes, I’d also like to add that I reinstalled the system during this time and updated the programs. But the build is still the same as it was originally - it’s X11.

I want to add that, for now, this issue persists up to v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439]. I also noticed an interesting detail on how to trigger it en masse — by launching multiple windows at the same time. Now you don’t even need to check anything; it’s clear that it occupies any of the corners or the center right from the start.
